security_frame.attacker: An agent able to issue AXI reads on the Caliptra subordinate interface while a write request from any agent is valid in the same cycle. No debug access and no physical access are required.
security_frame.precondition: The arbiter's persistent-priority bit r_pri favours the read channel, which is the state left behind by any completed write burst.
security_frame.input: A read request and a write request asserted in the same cycle with distinct AXI USER values.
security_frame.protected_asset: The AXI USER attribute of the granted request, which the soc_ifc allowlists treat as the authenticated requester identity for mailbox, fuse, TRNG and DMA accesses.
security_frame.security_property: Every attribute of a granted request must describe the same transaction: when the component-facing write output is 0 the addr, id and user outputs must all originate from the read channel, and when it is 1 they must all originate from the write channel.
security_frame.implemented_logic: src/axi/rtl/axi_sub_arb.sv:125 derives the USER select as ~(~r_win | w_dv), a function of both the grant decision and the write-valid signal, while addr, id and write at src/axi/rtl/axi_sub_arb.sv:129-133 are selected by r_win alone. A read grant taken while a write is valid therefore exports the write channel's USER value alongside the read channel's address and id.

security_feature_bypassed: Integrity of the AXI USER attribute used as the requester identity by the Caliptra mailbox, fuse, TRNG and DMA access-control allowlists
proof_goal: Show that a single axi_sub_arb instance can grant the read channel while exporting the concurrent write channel's USER value, and that the affected USER output reaches the soc_ifc allowlist comparisons.
invariant: For every cycle in which dv is asserted, the component-facing addr, id and user must all originate from the channel identified by the write output: write==0 implies the read channel, write==1 implies the write channel.
attacker_model: An agent that can issue AXI reads on the subordinate interface while a write from another agent, or from its own write channel, is valid in the same cycle. No debug access and no physical access are required.
minimum_attack_sequence: Complete a write burst so the arbiter's persistent-priority bit r_pri is set toward the read channel.
Assert a read request and a write request in the same cycle with distinct USER values.
Sample the component-facing write, addr, id and user outputs in that cycle.
controls: control_read_only: a lone read request must export the read channel's USER value.
control_write_only: a lone write request must export the write channel's USER value.
control_concurrent_write_priority: a concurrent request with priority on the write channel grants the write channel, whose own USER value is then correct.
expected_evidence: Structural gates confirming the USER select term differs from the addr, id and write select terms, and that the read grant is reachable while a write is valid.
Structural gates confirming the arbiter USER output reaches soc_req.user and that soc_req.user is compared against AXI_USER allowlists.
A simulation log in which three control cases report coherent attributes and the violating case reports a read grant carrying the write channel's USER value.
success_criteria: All three control cases pass, proving the checker is not vacuous.
Exactly one witness hit is observed and the script prints result=PASS and BUG_007_WITNESS_OBSERVED.
The script exits nonzero if any control fails or the witness is absent.
non_findings: This case does not claim a measured data disclosure over a full SoC boot; it proves the identity mismatch on the arbiter's component interface and identifies the allowlist comparisons that consume it.
This case does not claim the arbiter drops or corrupts the read data itself; rdata is unaffected.
This case does not assert how often the concurrent-request window occurs in a given integration; the attack complexity is rated high for that reason.
